COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
CRLR No. 110 of 2026
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J. 
1. Mrs. Monika Pant, learned counsel for the 
revisionist.
2. The instant criminal revision has been preferred 
for enhancement of the maintenance granted by the 
Family Court. As per the office report, there is a delay 
of 31 days. The delay is sufficiently explained and as 
such the delay condonation application is allowed.
3. Admit.
4. Learned counsel for the revisionist informed to 
this court that the respondent-husband also filed a 
revision i.e. Criminal Revision No. 894 of 2025 in which 
notices have been issued.
5. Taking into consideration that the dispute is 
nothing but appears to be a matrimonial dispute, 
therefore, the efforts may be made for their amicable 
settlement. 
6. In such view of the matter, let the learned counsel 
for the revisionist may inform to the counsel, who is 
representing the respondent-husband in the aforesaid 
revision.
7. List along with CRLR No. 894 of 2025 on 
26.02.2026.
8. On that day both the parties shall join the 
proceeding either physically or through V.C.
9. Learned counsel for the revisionist shall supply 
the copy of the revision to Mr. Saurabh Kumar Pandey 
during the course of the day.
 
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 17.02.2026
PR

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
CRLR No. 110 of 2026
CRLR No. 894 of 2025
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J. 
1. Mrs. Monika Pant, learned counsel for the
revisionist.
2. Mr. Tumul Nainwal, learned A.G.A. with Mrs. 
Sweta Badola Dobhal, learned Brief Holder for the 
State.
3. Mr. Saurabh Kumar Pandey, learned counsel for 
the respondent.
4. These are the two revisions, one filed by the wife 
and other one by the husband. The Family Court fixed 
interim maintenance of Rs. 30,000/-. There is one issue 
from their marriage and the child is 2 ½ years old. Both 
of them married in the year 2013. The husband is 
serving as Lt. Colonel in the Army and getting monthly 
salary of more than Rs. 2.30 lakhs. The interim 
maintenance as fixed by the Trial Court though is not 
reasonable and it has to be increased but learned 
counsel for the revisionist-wife submits that even the 
interim maintenance as fixed by the Family Court has 
not been paid to the revisionist.
5. Mr. Saurabh Pandey, who appears on behalf of 
the husband, submits that let an attempt be made for 
their amicable settlement and both the parties may be 
asked to be present on the next date. He also 
undertakes on instructions that by that time the arrear 
towards interim maintenance will also be paid by the 
husband by crediting the amount in the account of the 
revisionist-wife by tomorrow. The revisionist-wife shall 
provide the account details to Mr. Saurabh Pandey 
today itself.
6. Put up this matter on 25.03.2026.
7. On that day both the parties shall remain present 
in court.
 
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 26.02.2026
PR

CRLR No. 110 of 2026
With
CRLR No. 894 of 2026
Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Ms. Monika Pant, learned counsel for the 
petitioner.
2. Mr. Sandeep Sharma, learned A.G.A. for 
the State.
3. Mr. Saurabh Kumar Pandey, learned 
counsel for the respondent.
4. Both the parties were directed to appear 
before the Counsellor and the Counsellor, after 
counseling them submitted its report, thereafter, 
this Court also interact with both of them in the 
presence of father of the wife as well as in the 
presence of the counsel for half an hour and now 
this Court comes to the conclusion that at least 
two months’ time should be given to the 
husband to think over it so that thier
matrimonial life be restored. In such view of the 
matter the husband shall provide landline 
number and other contact number of his 
immediate boss, namely, Brigadier Vishwajeet 
Das so that wife may get update status of her 
husband. Both are directed to open their mobiles 
24 hours including whatsapp so they may share 
messages and free to contact through mobile.
5. This Court also advise both of them that 
they are the best person to resolve their 
matrimonial life and should focus to secure
future of their minor daughter who is about 2 
years seven months old. There are some issue of 
the wife and the husband who is present and 
undertakes that he will not repeat the wrong 
which he has done in the past and will not be in 
contact with other lady friends. 6. Today the husband handed over a draft of 
Rs. 1 lakh to the wife and undertake also to keep 
on paying the regular maintenance. 
7. Put up this matter on 02.06.2026 as part 
heard. On that day both the parties shall remain 
present in Court. 
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) 
17.04.2026
Parul

1. Ms. Monika Pant, learned counsel for the 
petitoiner.
2. Mr. Sandeep Sharma, learned A.G.A. for 
the State.
3. Mr. Saurabh Kumar Pandey, learned 
counsel for the respondent.
4. On the previous date, both the parties were 
directed to think over in order to resolve their 
dispute.
5. Today, wife joined the proceeding through 
VC.
6. Mr. Pandey apprise to this Court that the 
husband underwent with knee surgery. 
7. It has also been apprised that the arrears of 
maintenance which is more than Rs. 4 lakhs has 
not been paid.
8. In such view of the matter, husband/ 
revisionist is directed to clear the entire arrears 
positively within a month from today failing 
which on the next date necessary direction will 
be issued to deduct the amount from his regular 
salary.
9. List this case on 06.07.2026.
 
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)

Ms. Monika Pant, Advocate for the

2. Mr. Vikas Uniyal, A.G.A. for the State in 
CRLR No. 894 of 2025.
3. Revisionist (wife) is present before this 
Court today. Respondent (husband) is also 
present through V.C. before this Court today.
4. On the last date, the Coordinate Bench 
of this Court vide its order dated 02.06.2026 
had directed the respondent/husband to clear 
all arrears of maintenance.
5. Today, revisionist (wife) has submitted 
before this Court that respondent/husband  has not cleared all the arrears of maintenance 
and has paid only Rs.1 Lakh on 17.04.2026, 
which is much before the order passed by the 
Coordinate Bench of this Court.
6. Since, after passing of the order dated 
02.06.2026, respondent/husband has neither 
paid any arrears of maintenance nor has he 
paid the monthly interim maintenance, as
fixed by the Family Court concerned, as such,
this Court is left with no other option, but, to 
direct the office of Independent Armoured 
Brigade (Bhatinda Military Station), Army Pin￾908014 C/O 56 APO (through 56 Army Post 
Office) to deduct Rs. 3.5 Lakhs (Rupees Three 
Lakhs, Fifty Thousand), which has been 
accumulated as arrears till date and also to 
deduct Rs. 30,000/- on monthly basis, from 
the salary of respondent/husband and 
transfer the said amount to the account of the 
revisionist (wife), till further orders of this 
Court. The account details of the revisionist 
(wife) is as hereunder:-
Account Holder’s Name – Saroj Norki, 
Account No. 32112488867, IFSC –
SBIN0000646.
7. List this matter on 10.08.2026.
 (Alok Mahra J.) 06.07.2026
Ujjwal
